developments: Bitcoin slipped below $60,000 overnight, touching about $59,360 on Kraken, and traded near $60,380 at 06:35 UK, about 1.6% below the evening edition.
Grayscale's new 2x leveraged Zcash ETF fell more than 13% on its first day, The Block reported, and ZEC drifted to about $764, some 3.5% below the evening edition.
CFTC staff said bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins can count, after a haircut, towards a one-year operating-expense requirement for US derivatives venues, The Block reported.
briefing.changed: A little weaker than last night. The Asia session did not rescue Monday's fade: bitcoin broke below $60,000 for a while and has given back all of Monday's Nvidia jump, and ZEC kept sliding.
briefing.question: Did spot bitcoin ETF buyers return on Monday? Early aggregator figures point to heavy outflows, but they disagree and are unconfirmed.
briefing.watch: Confirmed Monday ETF flow figures this morning UK, US consumer confidence at 15:00 UK, then US PCE inflation on Wednesday at 13:30 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Bitcoin dips below $60,000 as Monday's rally fully unwinds
lead.standfirst: Bitcoin briefly fell under $60,000 overnight, giving back all of Monday's Nvidia-driven jump, while a new leveraged Zcash fund had a rough debut.
body: Bitcoin traded near $60,380 on Kraken at 06:35 UK, Kraken data showed, about 1.6% below the evening edition and roughly $4,100 under Monday's high of $64,520. It touched about $59,360 overnight, below its Monday open of about $61,200.
The move extended a fade that began in US trading on Monday, when bitcoin slipped back even as the Nasdaq held a gain of almost 7% on Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive.

Grayscale's head of research, Zach Pandl, wrote in a note on Monday that bitcoin and major altcoins looked oversold, The Block reported. He said bitcoin was 56% below its October 2025 peak after falling to about $55,000 on Saturday, that the bear market had lasted at least 411 days, and that crypto funds lost more than $2 billion last week.
In Zcash, Grayscale's 2x leveraged fund ZECX fell more than 13% to $28.60 on its first day on NYSE Arca, The Block reported. ZEC itself traded near $764 on Kraken.

Separately, CFTC staff said bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins can count towards an operating-expense requirement for US derivatives venues, The Block reported. Attention now turns to confirmed Monday ETF flows and Wednesday's PCE inflation data.

headline: Bitcoin dipped below $60,000 overnight and sits near $60,380, with Monday's rally fully reversed. Grayscale's new 2x Zcash ETF fell 13% on debut as ZEC slid to about $764.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, morning edition, Tuesday the twenty fourth of November. Bitcoin slipped below sixty thousand dollars overnight and now sits near sixty thousand four hundred, about one and a half percent lower than last night, with Monday's Nvidia jump fully undone. Grayscale says crypto looks oversold after a bear market of more than four hundred days. Zcash is down to about seven hundred and sixty five dollars, and Grayscale's new double leveraged Zcash fund fell thirteen percent on its first day. Watch Monday's ETF flows this morning, US consumer confidence at three this afternoon, and US inflation on Wednesday at half past one. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Bitcoin dips below $60,000 overnight, near $60,380
stories.why: Kraken showed bitcoin near $60,380 at 06:35 UK, down from about $61,350 at the evening edition, after an overnight low of about $59,360. The new evidence is that the Asia session extended Monday's US-hours fade rather than reversing it, taking bitcoin below its Monday open and back under the $60,000 level flagged last night.

note.read: Monday's spike now looks like short covering that has fully run out, leaving bitcoin back in the weak range of last week.
note.alt: A quiet overnight drift on thin volume may say little; the US session and ETF flows are the bigger test.
note.change: A sustained move back above $62,000 with ETF inflows would weaken this read; a break below Saturday's $55,000 low would strengthen it.

stories.title: Grayscale's 2x Zcash ETF falls 13% on debut; ZEC near $764
stories.why: Grayscale's ZECX, which aims for twice the daily return of its ZCSH spot Zcash fund, began trading on NYSE Arca on Monday and fell more than 13% to $28.60, The Block reported. Kraken showed ZEC near $764 at 06:35 UK, about 3.5% below the evening edition, with an overnight low near $742. A leveraged product gives US traders a new way to amplify ZEC moves in both directions.

note.read: The fund's fall mostly reflects ZEC giving back Monday's spike, magnified by 2x leverage, rather than a verdict on the product.
note.alt: Weak first-day demand could signal limited US appetite for leveraged ZEC exposure.
note.change: Rising assets in ZECX and ZCSH over the coming weeks would point to growing institutional interest.

stories.title: Grayscale calls crypto oversold after a 411-day bear market
stories.why: Grayscale's Zach Pandl wrote that bitcoin and major altcoins look oversold, The Block reported, with bitcoin 56% below its October 2025 peak and the bear market at least 411 days old, the longest in Grayscale's comparison. He cited more than $2 billion of crypto fund outflows last week and named AI-related uncertainty, including the Nvidia leadership saga and Anthropic's planned IPO, as the main near-term risk.
stories.caveat: This is the view of a fund issuer with an interest in crypto demand.

stories.title: CFTC staff let derivatives venues count bitcoin towards expense reserves
stories.why: CFTC staff said bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins can count, after a haircut, towards the one-year operating-expense requirement for clearing houses, swap venues and futures exchanges, The Block and CoinDesk reported. The advisory is not binding and crypto still does not count towards the separate liquidity requirement, so it is a small step towards treating crypto as a balance-sheet asset rather than a demand driver.

stories.title: Early figures point to heavy ETF outflows on Monday
stories.why: Aggregators PANews and Phemex reported about $570 million of net outflows from US spot bitcoin ETFs on Monday, a fifth straight day, led by BlackRock's IBIT. If confirmed, it would mean ETF holders sold into Monday's rally, which helps explain why bitcoin could not hold its gains.
stories.caveat: Unconfirmed: a KuCoin flash item gave a much smaller outflow of about $57 million for 23 November, so the figure is uncertain until Farside or issuer data are checked.

stories.title: Strive buys no bitcoin last week, holds 43,404 BTC
stories.why: Treasury company Strive made no bitcoin purchases last week, leaving its holdings at 43,404 BTC, Bitcoin Magazine reported. Alongside Strategy's small 457 BTC buy and Bitdeer selling all its output, it shows corporate buying has slowed while prices fall.

explained.title: Why a 2x fund can fall more than twice as far
body: A 2x leveraged ETF resets every day to deliver twice that day's move. It does not promise twice the move over a week or a month.

In choppy markets, daily resetting erodes value: a rise and fall of the same size leaves the fund lower than where it started, and the loss grows with volatility. That is why leveraged funds on volatile coins such as ZEC are usually treated as short-term tools.

investigating: How big were Monday's spot bitcoin ETF outflows? Aggregators disagree ($570 million against $57 million); Farside or issuer data will settle it.
Did Chainflip recover its stolen BTC after Monday's bounty deadline? Still no statement found; evidence would be a Chainflip update or on-chain movement of the 122.9 BTC.
Will US-hours selling continue on Tuesday? Evidence: bitcoin's move between the 14:30 UK open and the 21:00 UK close.
